title: Forgiven federal loans larger than the payroll on the tax return
question: A paycheck-protection loan was capped at two and a half months of payroll. Does the payroll each City-funded nonprofit told the IRS support the loan it got?
finding: For most it does: across 236 City-funded nonprofits the median loan implies 69% of the payroll on the borrower's return. But 7 loans imply at least 1.25 times the largest payroll the borrower reported for 2020 to 2022, and 4 imply 1.5 times or more, together $12.1 million; the widest gap is Filipino-American Development Foundation, whose $385,801 loan implies $1.9 million of yearly payroll against $792,725 on its return.
how: A first-round loan could not exceed 2.5 times average monthly payroll costs, so a loan of a given size needs yearly payroll costs of at least the loan divided by 2.5, times 12 (pay above $100,000 a person did not count, which makes this a floor). That floor is compared with the largest payroll (officer pay, other salaries, pension, benefits and payroll taxes, Form 990 Part IX lines 5 to 10) on any of the borrower's returns for tax years ending 2020 to 2022. Loans are matched to City payees by exact name; first-round loans of $25,000 or more only.
limits: The loan was sized on 2019 or early-2020 payroll and the earliest returns on file end in 2020, so an organisation that shrank sharply in 2020 can show a gap honestly. Housing and arts groups often employ staff through affiliates that file their own returns, which makes the parent's return look small. The return can also report pay on other lines. Every loan here was approved by a lender and most were forgiven by the SBA; this is a question to put to the borrower, not a finding.
